packages.caption: Backend packages: the API enqueues, the graph resolves an adapter
packages.alt: The API queues durable work and plans questions; the worker dispatches to graph code that uses application adapters and matching models.

components.caption: Runtime components: one queue separates the request from the work
components.alt: The console calls one API for scoring and drafting, while a database queue separates the request from background refresh and approved execution.

deployment.caption: Local deployment: one host, two processes and a loopback fixture
deployment.alt: On one development machine Vite proxies browser requests to FastAPI, and a separate worker leases SQLite work and can drive the optional loopback test board.

domain-classes.caption: Candidate, listing and match: the result holds neither input
domain-classes.alt: Search state retains the private candidate profile and a collection of pairs, each joining one listing to its score and explanation.

drafting-classes.caption: Draft and reports: three checks answer three questions
drafting-classes.alt: A tailored resume for one profile and job, with three separate reports: factuality, ATS readability and rendering.

application-classes.caption: Adapter contracts: a capability is granted, not inherited
application-classes.alt: The adapter prepares a request and returns a result that may carry evidence; implementing the adapter interface does not grant permission to submit.

object-example.caption: A synthetic packet: three identifiers answer three questions
object-example.alt: A saved reply belongs to the example application, but the packet retains its original question verdict and neither approval nor submission has occurred.

account-erd.caption: Account tables: dotted links are lookups, not foreign keys
account-erd.alt: Session records identify a user, and private profiles, saved matches and drafts carry owner identifiers that accessors check rather than SQL foreign keys.

workflow-erd.caption: Workflow tables: the question plan is stored JSON
workflow-erd.alt: A private application identifies its approval packet, which stores the question plan as JSON, while saved answers, events and optional evidence links use application identifiers rather than foreign keys.

storage.caption: Storage layout: private files sit apart from shared retrieval data
storage.alt: Each account has its own upload, draft and evidence directories, separate from the shared job retrieval data, application database and local account-token mailbox.

data-flow.caption: Discovery data flow: what moves, and who owns the result
data-flow.alt: Ranking combines facts from a private candidate profile with shared listing data and saves the resulting scores and reasons for that account.

composite.caption: Worker internals: a claimed item enters by one port, the packet leaves by the other
composite.alt: A lease supplies a work item to the worker's dispatcher, which delegates approved execution to a handler that restores the reviewed packet for the application graph.

profile.caption: Local stereotypes: labels for the document, not runtime grants
profile.alt: Two documentary stereotypes extend the UML Class and Component metaclasses; the mapped answer class and assist component illustrate the labels but are not their Python subclasses.

deployment-queued.caption: Queued deployment: PostgreSQL carries records and the queue
deployment-queued.alt: A browser reaches the static console build, which calls the API process over HTTPS. The API and the supervised worker share PostgreSQL; the worker alone writes the Chroma directory and the data volume, and only the worker opens a browser context.

identity-classes.caption: Account records: every private row names its owner
identity-classes.alt: User owns access tokens and a model credential, and owns a candidate profile with its optional equal-opportunity record. Audit events name an actor.

er-overview.caption: Logical entities: a case begins at a packet, not a listing
er-overview.alt: An account owns a profile. The profile produces matches and drafts; a listing is assessed in a match. A draft feeds a review packet addressed to a listing, the packet becomes an application case, and the case is executed as a work run.
